newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil off on futures and U.S. cargo concerns.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil off on futures and U.S. cargo concerns.

text.p: NWE gas oil eased on Friday on falling underlying futures and softening of premiums as the arrival in Europe of some 400,000 tonnes of north American gas oil draws closer.

The first of at least 11 north American gas oil cargoes are set to arrive in Europe toward the end of September and although most traders say booming pre-winter demand in Europe will easily soak up the extra volume, many predict premiums will suffer.
"Premiums will come under pressure, but I see them rebounding pretty quickly," one trader said. On average, traders are predicting $1 to $2 drop in premiums over the coming week.
German heating oil cargo premiums currently stand at Oct IPE +$7.0/+$7.50, cif Hamburg for first half October delivery against offers of Oct IPE +$9.0 for prompt material.
There was talk a number of Russian cargoes were also due to hit the region in the next week but this was not confirmed. Bids were seen at Oct IPE +$6.0, cif NWE for a prompt cargo.
Low sulphur was steady at Oct IPE +$16/+$17, CIF nwe. although no large cargoes appear to have traded for some time.
On the barge market, traders said the market was very quiet. Premiums were seen at Oct IPE +$9.50/+$10.50 for prompt and Oct IPE +$6.0/+$7.0 for first half October.
